messages:
Maria: Nightly alert — pset generator change in `prompt_ordering_v2` looks like it increased failure rate on the date-normalization and intent prompt buckets. +4.2% fail vs baseline overnight. summary: https://redwood.corp/evals/alerts/INF-4321 :eyes:
Aj: Link doesn't load for me, can you paste the small diff or key stats?
Maria: quick stats: baseline fail 7.8% -> now 12.0%. Regression concentrated in: date-normalization (from 5.1% -> 10.3%), intent-hierarchy (2.7% -> 4.6%). No model changes this deploy.
Devon: I pulled the promptset diff — main change was swapping example ordering and enabling `shuffle_examples=true` for a couple generators. Looks like we accidentally changed sample order for anchoring examples.
Laura: oof. That ordering can change few-shot priming behavior. Did we also change any punctuation normalization?
Devon: Only ordering + a small whitespace trim for the last example. Diff snippet:
```
- examples: [E1, E2, E3]
+ examples: shuffle([E1, E3, E2])  # shuffle_examples turned on
```
Samir: eval-bot, can you show per-prompt-case breakdown and a few raw generations for failed cases?
eval-bot: Automated report attached. Top 3 failing prompts with examples and model outputs: 
- date-normalization/009: expected `2024-03-05` got `Mar 5, 2024` (scoring: wrong-format)
- intent/045: expected `set_reminder` got `create_task`
- date-normalization/102: hallucinated timezone offset
Full CSV: https://redwood.corp/evals/results/INF-4321.csv
Maria: Thanks. Hypothesis: reordering changed the nearest-example bias so the model prefers a different formatting variant.
Aj: Two options: 1) revert ordering to previous canonical order (rollback PR) and rebaseline nightly; 2) rebaseline with the new ordering if product accepts the changed behavior. Product must approve semantics change.
Laura: Product (Laura) here — we did not intend a semantics change. We prefer keeping user-facing behavior stable. Approve rollback for stabilization :thumbsup:
Samir: I'll open a rollback PR now and run a canary evaluation against 1k samples. Tagging @eng-ml reviewers. PR: https://redwood.corp/repos/promptsets/pulls/725
Devon: For the long term we should add a deterministic seeding policy and an eval to detect ordering sensitivity. Maybe a unit test that permutes examples and checks variance.
Maria: Agreed. Also add a baseline test that runs the generator with both `shuffle_examples=true/false` and flags >1% delta.
Aj: Sounds good. For now, rollback + quick canary. If canary looks good, auto-promote to next nightly. 
Samir: Canary kicked off: `POST /internal/eval/canary` payload: `{
  "promptset": "prompt_ordering_v2",
  "variant": "rollback-ordering",
  "samples": 1000
}`
eval-bot: Canary results ready (1h). Fail rate rolled back to 8.1% (within noise of baseline). Marking incident INF-4321 resolved -> follow-up ticket INF-4322 created for ordering-sensitivity tests.
Maria: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident thread and notify customer-sig if any users saw this change.
Laura: Thanks — keep me posted if product needs to change any acceptance criteria.
Aj: Nice quick triage. I'll add a note to the prompt onboarding doc about ordering implications.
Samir: PR merged, will monitor next nightly.
Maria: closing the thread here, but leaving INF-4322 for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
